sentences.text: Deepak vs The State Of Haryana on 20 April, 2023

Bench: V. Ramasubramanian, Pankaj Mithal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2023
 (@ SLP(Crl.) No. 2256/2023)
 Deepak Appellant(s
 Versus
 State Of Haryana Respondent(
 O R D E R
Leave granted.

The appellant was implicated in a criminal complaint in FIR No.0019/2020 registered on 10.01.2020 for alleged offences under Sections 354, 370, 376, 506 read with Section 120-B IPC and Section 25 of the Arms Act.
The appellant was taken into custody on the next day namely 11.01.2020.
He is in jail for the past nearly three years and three months.
The chargesheet was already filed and out of sixteen witnesses, nine witnesses have already been examined.
More particularly, the prosecutrix has been examined.
Therefore considering the above facts, we are of the view that the appellant can be released on bail at this stage.
Therefore the appeal is allowed and the appellant is directed to be released on bail subject to such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
.......................J. ( V. RAMASUBRAMANIAN ) .......................J. ( PANKAJ MITHAL ) NEW DELHI;
